question.problem:
The matrix $A$ and vectors ${b}_{1}$, ${b}_{2}$, ${b}_{3}$ are given below. Which of the vectors lie in $\text{Null}(A)?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
A vector $b$ lies in $\text{Null}(A)$ if $Ab=0.$ So, we need to compute the product of $A$ and each of the given vectors and check whether it is equal to $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A{b}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\ne 0\,\times  \\ A{b}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\ne 0\,\times  \\ A{b}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 0 \\ 8\end{aligned}]\ne 0\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, none of the vectors lies in $\text{Null}(A).$
